items.title: Canonical reasoning-effort ladder mapped per model to each provider wire format
items.summary: Define one canonical effort scale (none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh) and a single resolve_effort() in inference-core that every provider adapter calls: clamp the request to the nearest weaker level the model supports, then map it to the provider vocabulary (OpenAI/Azure reasoning effort, Anthropic thinking budget, Codex reasoning_effort, later Gemini thinking level). Start with a static per-model table and move it into the model record (R-t3-09-05) later; keep the composer's Auto / Raskt svar / Dyp research dial as presets over the canonical scale.
items.whyItMatters: Budget/Balance/Genius defaults are mostly OpenAI-family models, and that route currently sends no reasoning effort at all, so the user's depth choice is ignored on the most-used path. This is a code-verified gap with a small, well-understood fix that six of twelve references implement.

others: codexagent (032, best declared per-model ladder with descriptions)
deepseek (092, refuses unsupported values before dispatch)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: An EFFORT_LADDER plus named per-generation wire vocabularies and clamp_effort() that picks the nearest weaker supported level instead of sending a value that returns 400; capability probes are cached per (model, base_url). The composer renders only the levels the selected model declares. [SRC for Hermes/Codex/DeepSeek]

evidence: grep of inference-core/src/provider/openai.rs finds no reasoning_effort (verified read-only); only codex_subscription.rs sets it
verevonToday.gap: Quick/Standard/Deep profiles produce an Anthropic thinking budget and a Codex low/high effort only. The OpenAI and Azure chat path sends no effort, there is no per-model declared ladder, no clamp-to-nearest rule, and no per-role or per-surface cap.

items.approach: Model Plane: add an Effort enum and resolve_effort(model, requested, role_cap) in inference-core/src/provider (shared by openai.rs, anthropic.rs, codex_subscription.rs); wire OpenAI/Azure reasoning models first and declare 'none' for non-reasoning ids such as gpt-4o-mini; keep model-gateway/src/thinking.rs profiles as the preset layer that picks a canonical level instead of a raw budget. Log the clamp on the run and show the cost multiplier for high levels. Composer reads supported levels from the model record once R-t3-09-05 exists.
dependencies: R-t3-09-05 model record (optional; can start with a static table)
items.risks: Higher effort raises cost and latency; tie default levels to budget posture and show the multiplier. Do not send effort to models that reject the parameter.

alreadyPlanned.where: Named as a gap in the v-modelplane baseline (no OpenAI reasoning-effort mapping); no plan found

items.title: Org and role model entitlements: Control Plane decides, Model Plane enforces at admission
items.summary: Give the refused allowed_models policy field a real owner: a Control Plane entitlement policy (org, role, group, plan) with allow/deny model lists, maximum effort, admin default model/effort per surface, and an explain endpoint for one member's effective access. Model Plane receives the resolved entitlement in the auth context, filters ListModels, and refuses disallowed models at admission with a typed reason, never silently substituting.
items.whyItMatters: Enterprise buyers expect to restrict expensive or non-EU models per role. The code itself flags this hole: the gateway refuses the allowlist by name because no service owns it, so operators currently cannot restrict models at all.

others: claude (152, per-role effort caps, most permissive role wins)
codexagent (045, 043, plan lists and access programs as catalogue data)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 5 of 12 sources; table-stakes (judgement: web-only sources expose little internals)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Admins set starting model, reasoning level and speed separately per surface; new models are off by default for enterprise; roles are additive (union of allows) and the most permissive effort cap wins; a Model Test tool shows a member's effective access. [DOC for ChatGPT, SRC for Claude desktop and Codex]

evidence: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/grpc.rs:148-160 (verified: allowed_models is the only policy field with no owner and is refused by name)
verevonToday.gap: No per-org or per-role model allowlist, no role-level effort cap, no admin default per surface, no effective-access explainer. The privacy-tier floor in admission already fails closed but is not an entitlement system.

items.approach: Control Plane: policy schema {subject, allow_models[], deny_models[], max_effort, default_model, default_effort} with resolution (union of role allows, intersect with plan, most permissive effort cap) and an explain API. Model Plane: extend mp-authctx claims to carry the resolved entitlement; inference-core filters ListModels and enforces in admission next to the privacy-tier floor. Frontend Plane: admin page beside the router-policy page (apps/gateway/src/domains/router_policy.rs). The entitlement can only narrow access; it must never widen an owner-plane ACL or a Space's rights.
dependencies: Control Plane policy schema and API
items.planeOwner: Control Plane (policy) with Model Plane (enforcement) and Frontend Plane (admin UI)
items.risks: Resolution order must be documented and tested; entitlement must not widen Space or owner-plane ACLs; stale cached entitlements could allow a revoked model.

alreadyPlanned.where: The code comment acknowledges the gap (grpc.rs:148-157) but no plan was found

items.title: Prompt-cache stability tiers, lineage-scoped cache keys and a measured hit rate
items.summary: Turn on and measure what is already built: enable the OpenAI stable-prefix prompt order in staging, record cache_read/cache_write tokens and a cache-miss reason per route, then enforce stable-to-volatile segment tiers in prompt_context (org and Space blocks in the shared prefix, per-user memory and time late), add a prompt_cache_key derived from org, compaction-lineage root and tools hash, and use rolling Anthropic cache_control breakpoints with a block limit.
items.whyItMatters: Cache savings are the largest cost and latency lever for long agent runs and Space-heavy prompts and directly feed the Budget posture the router depends on, yet no cache hit has been measured on any route and the OpenAI-side reordering is off by default.

others: cursor (105, 076, rolling four-breakpoint rule and prefix-reusing summary calls)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A three-tier system prompt (stable, context, volatile) rebuilt only on compaction keeps the longest prefix byte-identical for a session; the provider cache key is scoped to the compression-lineage root so compaction does not reset it while branches and delegates get their own scope; Anthropic breakpoints are rolled (last message always marked, older ones dropped). [SRC]

evidence: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/prompt_context.rs:1-23 (verified: stable-prefix order gated by MODEL_GATEWAY_CACHE_STABLE_PROMPT_ORDER, off unless set)
verevonToday.gap: Anthropic cache_control is applied to tools, system and history, but the OpenAI stable-prefix order is off by default, no cache hit has been measured on any route per the cache audit (DOC), there is no lineage-scoped cache key, no cache-miss reasons, and memory or time blocks are not placed in a volatile tail by contract.

items.approach: model-gateway prompt_context: assign each slot a stability class and render in tier order; turn the OpenAI order on by default once a staging A/B shows hits; add prompt_cache_key = hash(org, lineage_root, tools_hash) in the OpenAI adapter and rolling breakpoints in anthropic.rs; add cache_miss_reason (ttl_expired, prefix_changed, tools_changed) to the usage event and show it in the Work panel. Needs a compaction lineage id from Session Core. Do not reintroduce a semantic answer cache (langcache.rs is a deliberate tombstone).
dependencies: compaction lineage id from Session Core
per-provider ZDR contract check for provider-side caching
items.risks: ZDR turns must not use provider-side caching where that implies retention (check each provider contract); reordering blocks can change answer behaviour, so A/B on recorded journeys first.

alreadyPlanned.where: Built but undeployed OpenAI-route cache items per the CACHE_COMPACTION_AUDIT (v-planned-decisions baseline line 212); no measurement yet

items.title: Gemini provider family (Vertex, EU region) with tool-schema sanitising and a Gemini prompt profile
items.summary: Add a third ModelFamily for Gemini in inference-core: a native generateContent/streamGenerateContent adapter on Vertex AI in an EU region, thinking-level mapping from the effort ladder, thought-signature replay through the replay envelope (R-t3-09-07), and a decorator that sanitises tool JSON Schemas to the Gemini subset. Add a minimal Gemini prompt/tool profile and re-enable the soft-deleted catalogue row, then expose Gemini in the picker and router table (long-context and perception roles).
items.whyItMatters: Gemini and its long-context and video strengths are named in the product goal (Antigravity capabilities), and five of twelve references ship Gemini or a multi-vendor lineup. Without it Verevon cannot route perception or long-context roles to the best model.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: web-perplexity (web-perplexity-web-product-082) for the lineup; antigravity (082) for Gemini thinking levels
others: hermes (098, sanitises tool schemas for Gemini and Kimi)
cursor (075, 104, family detection and prompt variants)

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: One picker across vendors with a Best auto-router and a per-model Thinking toggle; native adapters per vendor registered as provider families with a full capability record and residency; schema sanitisers per strict provider. [DOC for lineup, SRC for sanitiser and prompt variants]

evidence: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/inference-core/src/provider/mod.rs:471 (verified: ModelFamily has only OpenAiCompatible and Anthropic)
apps/Model Plane/rust/go/services/capability-core/migrations/0013_privacy_tier_columns.up.sql:23 (Gemini seed row soft-deleted because no adapter can serve it)

The per-family prompt and tool variants half of this item has no baseline record (status unknown): check model-gateway prompt assembly for branching by provider or model family and whether tool schemas are sanitised per provider.

Do not route privacy-floored or ZDR turns to Gemini until Vertex terms are attested.

items.title: Model record v2 served by inference-core, validated at admission and rendered by a searchable picker
items.summary: Replace the thin ModelDescriptor with a versioned ModelRecord (context window, max output, input modalities, reasoning ladder and default, verbosity support, service tiers, lifecycle, price ref, privacy tier, residency, availability, prompt profile id) owned by inference-core and returned whole by ListModels. Use it for a PreparedCall step in admission (validate effort, modalities and model/provider pairing before any network call, with typed refusals and suggestions), and render it in a Solid picker with fuzzy search, server-persisted favourites and recents, a Legacy fold and locked-model reasons. Later, load the catalogue from a signed, versioned artifact with an on-disk last-good copy.
items.whyItMatters: One record drives the picker, effort control, context budgeting, router decisions and entitlements; adding Gemini or a new GPT generation becomes a data change. The grouped picker without search will not scale once Gemini and BYO endpoints land.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: codexagent (codexagent-029, 098) for the record; t3code (004) for the picker; claude desktop (069) for signed distribution; deepseek (036) for prepared calls
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 4 of 12 for the record, 4 of 12 for distribution, 3 of 12 for prepared calls, 2 of 12 for the picker; common
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: An embedded, remotely refreshed models.json with about 40 fields per model projected to clients by model/list; a signed catalogue with a signature sidecar, size caps and a custom URL; a frozen prepared call bound to the adapter after validation; a picker with provider rail, tokenised fuzzy search, favourites first and a collapsible Legacy section. [SRC]

verevonToday.gap: ListModels returns only id, provider, modality, streaming, feature families, privacy tier and residency. No context window, max output, ladder, service tiers, lifecycle, price or plan gating, so the SPA cannot gate controls per model. There is no general prepared-call validation, no versioned or signed catalogue, and the picker has no search, favourites, recents, legacy fold or locked-model explanation.

items.approach: mp-contracts: extend the inference-core ListModels proto with the record fields (version it so the gateway passes it through uninterpreted); seed from the existing feature list and cost-core price ids; add a startup test that every routable model has a complete record. inference-core admission: prepare(req, catalogue) -> PreparedCall or typed Refusal, allowing an unverified-but-allowed state. Frontend Plane: Solid popover component with favourites and recents stored per user through the gateway; locked entries rendered from R-t3-09-02 reasons, availability from R-t3-09-08. Last phase: catalogue loader with signature verification, ETag cache and a compiled-in floor; RoutingPolicy remains the overlay.
dependencies: signing key management for the signed catalogue phase
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (record, admission, catalogue) with Frontend Plane (picker)
items.risks: Records drift from provider reality (mitigate with a startup probe and test); over-strict validation can block valid provider ids; a bad catalogue push could hide every model, so require schema validation, staged rollout and a compiled-in floor.

items.title: Role table and purpose tags for every inference call, plus multimodal input routing
items.summary: Add a role dimension to RoutingPolicy (chat, planner, worker, subagent:type, title, follow_ups, verification_judge, compaction, memory_extract, vision, scheduled) mapping each role to a model or intent mode, effort and fallback, and replace the hard-coded gpt-4o-mini constants with role lookups. Carry a role/purpose tag in the inference request so metering, cost and ZDR audit can attribute auxiliary calls. On top, add a gateway pre-processor driven by the model record: native image parts when the model accepts them, describe-first through the vision role when it does not, with per-request image budgets and a visible image-offload notice.
items.whyItMatters: Background inference gets cheaper and policy-consistent, and Verevon can route perception or long-context subagents to the best provider (for example Gemini for video) without touching the main loop. Multimodal parity lets images and documents join agent tool loops on any routed model.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: hermes (hermes-architecture-and-surfaces-099 roles, 104 image input mode); deepseek (044, 157 purpose tags)
others: antigravity (084, ModelTier per subagent and system job)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 6 of 12 for role slots (common); 4 of 12 for multimodal routing (common); 1 of 12 for purpose tags (unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: auxiliary.<task>.{provider, model, effort} for about 20 side tasks resolved through the same runtime resolver as the main model; GenerateOptions.purpose lets adapters attach transport metadata without changing model input; decide_image_input_mode picks native versus describe-first once per turn from the main model capability. [SRC]

evidence: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/sse.rs:7839-7894 (verified: TITLE_MODEL, FOLLOW_UPS_MODEL, VERIFICATION_JUDGE_MODEL are gpt-4o-mini constants)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/inference-core/src/provider/vision.rs (image generation, analysis and OCR provider; wiring into the chat tool loop not verified)
verevonToday.gap: Side tasks exist but their models are constants and the planner resolves its own model; there is no editable role table. Whether calls carry a purpose tag, whether non-vision models get a describe pre-step, and whether image budgets or offload notices exist are unknown (no baseline record): check how attachments reach tool loops in model-gateway.

items.approach: inference-core: role enum and a role-to-route table inside RoutingPolicy (routing_policy.rs), resolved through the same intent/fallback path so the privacy floor and ZDR apply equally; default every role to today's constant so nothing changes on day one. Add role/purpose to the inference proto and record it in the metered decorator and cost entries. model-gateway: replace the constants in sse.rs and deep_research.rs; attachment pre-processor reading input_modalities from the model record, Data Plane documents passed as handles resolved by a read tool. Admin edits the role table in the existing router-policy page (apps/gateway/src/domains/router_policy.rs).
items.risks: Misconfigured roles can raise cost (default to current constants); describe-first loses detail (show which path was used); do not send org identifiers to providers unless contracts allow it.

items.title: Per-step routing decision and model continuity: resolver, lifecycle successors and a reasoning replay envelope
items.summary: Implement the planned step-level RoutingDecision {requested, resolved model, provider, effort, reason, complexity, budget posture} in inference-core, persist it on every run step in Session Core, and surface model and reason in the served-by line with an optional routing-feedback control. Build one resolve_model() with fixed precedence (explicit, thread last step, Space default, user last used, org default, intent default) that chat, Do, scheduled runs and subagents all call; add lifecycle states and successor ids so retired model ids resolve to successors with a model_switched event; insert a notice only when the provider family changes. Capture Anthropic signature and redacted thinking blocks (and later Gemini thought signatures) in a ReplayEnvelope stored with the step and replay them only to the matching adapter and model.
items.whyItMatters: Serves the DeepSeek-style transparency goal, gives the router-policy page real data to tune Budget/Balance/Genius, and protects saved threads, agents and scheduled runs from provider model retirements. Replay is required for correct multi-turn tool use with thinking models and is a blocker for Gemini.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: hermes (097 reasoning replay, 093 single resolver); cursor (073, 108 routed model); codexagent (035 lifecycle and upgrade target); deepseek (094, 134 mid-thread notice)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: replay 4 of 12 (common); routed-model stream 2 of 12, lifecycle 3 of 12, switching semantics 2 of 12, layered defaults 2 of 12 (differentiators)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: reasoning_carriers stores opaque reasoning as typed private records lifted back only for the matching route, with fingerprints of signature-rejected blocks excluded on retry; the agent stream emits routed_model with a display name; the catalogue declares upgrade {model, migration note, retirement_at} and a thread switches automatically after retirement; a durable notice tells the new model earlier turns came from another model. [SRC]

evidence: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/sse_events.rs:39-60 (ServedBy carries provider deployment, residency and privacy tier but no resolved model or reason)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/inference-core/src/config.rs:83 (only a comment about a retired Cohere model name)
verevonToday.gap: Routing is request-level only (step-level RoutingDecision is planned), the served-by line has no model id or reason, signed thinking cannot be replayed, and there is no routing feedback. Lifecycle handling, per-message or per-thread model storage in Session Core, behaviour when a saved model is no longer routable, and a single resolver for chat, Do and scheduled runs have no baseline record (unknown); the Space default does not exist.

items.approach: inference-core: RoutingDecision per call plus a resolve_model(ctx) used by every surface; lifecycle {state, retire_at, successor_id} in the model record (R-t3-09-05). Session Core: extend the step schema with the route and an optional ReplayEnvelope {adapter, model, blocks}; skip persisting envelopes on ZDR turns. model-gateway: routed_model / model_switched SSE events, a small router-feedback endpoint, an org setting to show tier names only; strip replay state and add a notice on family change. Application Plane projection carries the Space default; it can only select among already-entitled models.
items.risks: Reasoning content retention must follow ZDR; automatic successor mapping can change cost or behaviour (record it per run and show it); notices consume tokens and can break caches (insert only on family change); exposing model names may conflict with abstraction choices.

alreadyPlanned.where: Step-level RoutingDecision is planned in docs/MODEL_PLANE_IMPROVEMENTS_2026.md section 9 (v-modelplane baseline line 245)

items.title: Resilient routing: failure vocabulary, credential pools, benching, usage-limit and refusal fallbacks, provider health
items.summary: Extend the shipped fallback chain in inference-core with a closed failure code set (auth, quota, rate limit, context too long, server, timeout, refusal, empty response) carrying retry_after, per-route retry policy, pooled deployments or credentials with model-scoped cooldowns, and benching of a failed primary until its declared reset. Add declared fallback models for usage-limit exhaustion with a switch-back at reset_at (opt-in when it crosses from a user subscription to platform billing), a policy-owned refusal fallback that records the original model and is undone on rewind or edit, and a per-provider health map exposed through ListModels so the picker greys unavailable routes with the reason.
items.whyItMatters: Fewer failed answers and stalled agent runs during provider incidents or quota exhaustion, which matters most for unattended scheduled agents and Azure deployment quotas. The subscription route currently stops at its limit with a typed message but no alternative.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: hermes (hermes-architecture-and-surfaces-095, 094 failover and credential pools); codexagent (036 usage-limit fallback and switch-back); claude (112 reversible refusal fallback); t3code (002, 050 provider health snapshot)
others: deepseek (126, 095 closed failure vocabulary and per-route retry modes)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: try_activate_fallback() rebuilds the client in place; cooldowns follow the provider-declared reset (exponential 60 s to 4 h when absent); credential pools rotate on plan-limit 429s before switching provider; limit errors carry reset_at, blocked model and fallback models, and the client announces switches and switch-backs; a model_refusal_fallback message switches the model and remembers the original. [SRC]

verevonToday.gap: A fallback chain with bounded retries and retry-after, typed context overflow, and typed subscription refusals with a reset time exist. Missing: credential pool, reset-aware benching, failover on the subscription route, automatic fallback model and switch-back at limit, org-quota fallback. Refusal-driven rerouting and whether provider health or quota state reaches /v1/models have no baseline record (unknown).

items.approach: inference-core fallback.rs: add the failure enum and per-route retry policy, a cooldown map keyed by (credential, model), benching with reset_at, and reroute events written into the RoutingDecision (R-t3-09-07). Every hop is filtered through the privacy floor, entitlements and cost gates. subscription route: declared fallback models plus a user consent setting for platform billing. Provider health map feeds the model record availability field and the picker. Refusal fallback lists live in RoutingPolicy.
dependencies: user consent setting for subscription-to-platform fallback
items.risks: Failover can silently cross privacy or cost lines (gate and display every hop); falling back from a user subscription to platform billing must be opt-in; stale health data can hide a working route (short-lived cheap probes); safety rerouting must always be disclosed.

alreadyPlanned.where: BKL #25 multi-provider auth-profile failover (docs/verevon_CHAT_PARITY_BACKLOG.md, v-modelplane baseline line 349)

items.title: Cost by token category, live credit meter, quota display and a context ring
items.summary: Extend the usage record with disjoint uncached input, cache read, cache write, output and reasoning tokens plus role/tool attribution, price each category in cost-core, and aggregate per turn, per subagent and per thread for the answer details popover and Work panel. Add the planned live credit meter fed by cost-core, per-model or per-family remaining quota with reset time from Control quotas, and a pre-run price confirmation above a threshold. Add a per-model compaction policy in the model record and a context ring with a manual Compact action driven by a context snapshot event.
items.whyItMatters: Users and admins see spend before and during long agent runs, which is the main fear with autonomous agents, and it delivers the maximum-information, transparent goal. Context pressure becomes visible instead of silent.

The inference-core metering decorator is reported built but not deployed (baseline DOC, ledger 2026-10-06).

Frontend Plane: render in the existing answer details popover and Work panel, add the ring to the composer. Label all figures as estimates and reconcile with Azure actual cost.

items.title: Declarative provider registry and bring-your-own connections
items.summary: Turn provider registration from environment configuration into data: a ProviderProfile (wire protocol, base and models URL, auth kind, compat switches, retry and timeout budgets, residency, privacy tier) stored by inference-core, added through a schema-generated admin form, with model discovery that proposes entries without mutating config until saved and an admin overlay (custom model ids, hide, reorder, unverified capability overrides). Then generalise the ChatGPT-subscription pattern into BYO connections held by Integration Core (API key, cloud role or helper command for Bedrock, Vertex, Azure Foundry, or a customer gateway), referenced by opaque connection id, with per-connection routing so a user or org can hold several connections of one provider.
items.whyItMatters: Enterprise and sovereign customers can add their own gateway, on-prem endpoint or cloud tenancy without a Verevon release, and heavy users can bring their own keys. It also covers the local-model need in a form appropriate for a cloud product.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: hermes (hermes-architecture-and-surfaces-091, 41 overridable provider profiles); claude desktop (claude-product-ux-107, claude-runtime-architecture-072 for BYO cloud accounts and helper credentials with TTL)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: registry 5 of 12 (common); BYO 6 of 12 (table-stakes); multi-instance 1 of 12; curation 2 of 12
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A ProviderProfile dataclass per provider with api mode, auth type, base and models URLs and error classification, overridable by a user profile of the same name; BYO credentials come from key, cloud role or a helper script with TTL and silent refresh, with health probes on save, and platform and customer credentials never fall back to each other. [SRC]

verevonToday.gap: Providers come from environment configuration (INFERENCE_PROVIDER_ORDER plus fixed adapters). Only the user-owned ChatGPT subscription route exists as a connection; there is no admin-defined provider record, compat switches, discovery, add-provider UI, API-key BYOK, customer cloud account or customer gateway. Whether a user or org can hold several connections of one provider, and any per-org model visibility beyond the router-policy table, have no baseline record (unknown).

items.approach: inference-core: provider-profile table with secrets referenced, never stored; discovery calls GET /models; profiles flow into the same fallback chain, privacy-tier gate and metered decorator. Customer-declared profiles default to the lowest privacy tier and no ZDR claim until attested. Integration Core: new credential kinds and short-lived token minting per call; Model Plane receives only an opaque connection id. cost-core: customer-billed flag. Frontend Plane: schema-annotated settings form. Phase 1 registry plus curation, phase 2 BYO.
dependencies: Integration Core credential kinds and token minting
items.risks: Unverified endpoints can claim residency or ZDR they do not have; customer endpoints may log prompts; confusing which account paid (show the connection on the served-by line); wrong capability overrides cause failures (mark unverified and log).

items.title: Router tuning loop: eval gate for RoutingPolicy changes, experiment ids and opt-in best-of-N
items.summary: Add a Model Plane eval job (Go durable tier) that runs a fixed task suite per (role, candidate model, effort) and records quality, cost and latency; require a passing comparison against the current table before a production org's RoutingPolicy edit is accepted, and publish results in the router-policy page. Generalise RoutingPolicy storage in Session Core into a typed config overlay with versions and a closed list of overridable keys, and stamp the overlay version and experiment ids on every run. As a later phase, add opt-in best-of-N: fork one turn to N routes with a cost cap, record the user's preferred answer and reasons, and feed that into the evals.
items.whyItMatters: The router is a core Verevon idea and the routing table is already runtime-editable, so it needs evidence to be safe to change and to justify defaults to customers. Preference data and experiment attribution make tuning empirical.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: codexagent (codexagent-agent-runtime-and-models-091 model-migration playbook); antigravity (091 best-of-N battle mode, 090 experiment overrides)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 3 of 12 for evals (differentiator); 2 of 12 for remote config; 1 of 12 for best-of-N (unique)

verevonToday.gap: Only the routing table is runtime-editable; prompts, loop budgets and defaults need a deploy and no experiment ids are stamped on runs. Whether the Model Plane eval-lab covers routing changes or any RoutingPolicy edit is gated on an evaluation has no baseline record (unknown). Side-by-side comparison is absent (searched compareModels, arena and side-by-side in the SPA and model-gateway; none found).

items.approach: Go durable tier: eval job over a task suite, results stored with an eval id; Session Core: versioned config overlay; gateway PUT for RoutingPolicy requires a stored eval id for production orgs. Refresh suites only from anonymised, consented, non-ZDR traces. Best-of-N: model-gateway fan-out with cost cap and confirmation, preference records in Session Core, Solid split view; opt-in only and the cost shown.
items.risks: Eval suites drift from real usage; best-of-N multiplies cost; config sprawl (keep a closed key list); never use ZDR traces.

alreadyPlanned.where: Eval architecture proposed in docs/MODEL_PLANE_IMPROVEMENTS_2026.md section 19 (v-modelplane baseline line 329)

items.title: Second-order latency and cache levers: speed tier, prewarm, cache-preserving in-band changes, Responses continuation
items.summary: After the cache and effort basics are measured, add optional levers in this order: a user-facing speed tier (Standard or Fast) declared in the model record and mapped to provider priority processing with a cost multiplier in cost-core; a prewarm call on composer focus (connection warm-up first, cache priming only if measured to pay) with deadline-based optional context sources and a context-status block; append-only in-band updates for changed prompts, effort and added tools, with background forks reusing the exact parent prefix; and, last, an OpenAI Responses adapter mode with incremental continuation for non-ZDR turns.
items.whyItMatters: Lower time to first token and cost on long sessions and connector-heavy threads. Plumbing already exists for the priority tier on the Codex route, and turn_timing gives a baseline to prove any gain.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: codexagent (034 service tiers, 038 Responses WebSocket); cursor (134, 110 prewarm and progressive hydration); deepseek (037, 038 in-history updates)
others: hermes (103 time-bounded fast windows, 058 cache-parity review forks)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: speed tier 3 of 12, in-band changes 3 of 12 (differentiators); prewarm 1 of 12, Responses WebSocket 1 of 12 (unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Per-model service_tiers with multipliers and a default tier; a request-header tool diff that emits one developer message instead of rewriting the tool list; prewarm_request mirroring a run request without an action; previous_response_id continuation with HTTPS fallback. [SRC]

evidence: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/latency_levers.rs:1-20 (existing env kill-switch pattern for latency levers)
verevonToday.gap: A prefer_priority_service_tier flag exists (Codex route, some internal gateway paths) but there is no user-facing speed control, no tier on platform OpenAI routes and no cost multiplier. Prewarm, append-only prompt or tool updates, parent-prefix reuse by background calls, and Responses continuation have no baseline record (a grep for prewarm and previous_response_id in Model Plane Rust found nothing): check how a mid-thread connector or skill addition changes the tool list.

items.approach: Follow the latency_levers.rs kill-switch pattern for each lever. Speed tier: model-record service_tiers plus composer toggle, price in cost-core. Prewarm: model-gateway endpoint plus deadline-bounded context sources, using turn_timing to prove a gain. In-band changes: header diffing (system_hash, tools_hash, effort) in prompt_context, enabled per model only where tested. Responses mode: optional adapter flag, rebuildable from Session Core history and disabled on ZDR turns.
items.risks: Cost surprises from the fast tier (show the multiplier); prewarm cache-priming spends tokens; provider-held state (previous_response_id) conflicts with ZDR and durable Session Core history, so restrict to non-ZDR turns; provider-specific in-band semantics.

dropped.reason: Not a fit: Verevon is a hosted cloud web product, the self-hosted Needle attempt was cancelled after measured poor quality, and on-prem or sovereign needs are served by customer endpoints in the provider registry (R-t3-09-10).

Not a fit: provider-native web search inside the model call would bypass Quarry, which owns web execution and capture (Model proposes, Quarry executes); web research is covered in the research category.

strengthsToKeep: Budget/Balance/Genius intent routing combines task complexity with the org's cost-core budget posture, a tool-use floor and a fallback ladder, and is runtime-editable through RoutingPolicy with an admin page; more adaptive than the fixed presets in most references (apps/Model Plane/rust/services/inference-core/src/provider/intent.rs, routing_policy.rs:127-222, apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/router_policy.rs).

Per-turn privacy-tier and residency floor (global, eu_resident, zdr_contractual, sovereign) is enforced before any network call and fails closed, and fallback hops respect it; no reference goes beyond warning (apps/Model Plane/rust/services/inference-core/src/config.rs:259-283, provider/fallback.rs:505-700).

User-owned ChatGPT subscription route keeps the OAuth token only in Integration Core and shows Model Plane an opaque connection id, with typed refusals for usage limit, reauth, rate limit and context too long; equal to Hermes on the idea and stricter on token custody (inference-core/src/provider/codex_subscription.rs, model-gateway/src/subscription_failure.rs).

Provider-neutral seam: a provider trait that declares its own ModelFamily, a metered decorator intended to cover every RPC, and a typed SSE event stream with server-stamped provenance that omits unknown fields instead of faking them (inference-core/src/provider/mod.rs:471, metered.rs:1-8, model-gateway/src/sse_events.rs:20-80). Caveat: the metering decorator is reported built but not deployed.

Structured outputs work on OpenAI, Anthropic (tool or instruction) and the subscription route (inference-core/src/provider/openai.rs:459-486, anthropic.rs:726-731, codex_subscription_tools.rs:15-33); gap is only a rejection memo for json_object-only MaaS endpoints.
Verbosity dial (concise, balanced, detailed) is shipped on every route (model-gateway/src/verbosity.rs, apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/dashboard/home/DashboardComposer.tsx:169-173).

Cost is never fabricated: cost-core prices are null when unknown and the subscription route says included in the subscription; cache creation and read tokens are priced (model-gateway/src/pricing.rs:206-257).

Assembled-context inspector (tokens per segment versus budget) is more detailed than any reference, and real BPE token counting plus typed context overflow exist (apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/chat/components/ChatPanels.tsx:571-720, apps/Model Plane/rust/crates/mp-tokens/src/lib.rs:1-5, inference-core/src/provider/overflow.rs:100).

Features no reference has in this category: fine-tuning jobs (model-gateway/src/finetune_routes.rs), logprob-based certainty (inference-core/src/provider/logprobs.rs) and TOON compact encoding (apps/Model Plane/rust/crates/mp-toon/src/lib.rs).

EU-resident Azure deployments of OpenAI, Claude and MaaS models with a residency and privacy tier on every registered provider give residency coverage most references lack (inference-core/src/config.rs:286-326).
